# PowerModeSlider — Copilot Instructions

A Windows 11 system-tray app (WinUI 3 / Windows App SDK, .NET 10) for switching power
modes via a slider flyout. Solution: `PowerModeSlider.slnx`.

## Projects

- **`PowerModeLib/`** — Plain `net10.0` class library. Zero UI/WinUI dependencies. Wraps
  the documented `powrprof.dll` power-mode P/Invokes (`PowerGet/SetUserConfiguredAC/DCPowerMode`).
  `PowerMode` is a `static` class exposing mode GUIDs and `TrySet*`/`Get*` helpers. APIs
  require Windows 11 (build 22000); guard with `PowerMode.IsSupported()` and the
  `[SupportedOSPlatform("windows10.0.22000")]` attribute.
- **`KeepAwakeLib/`** — Plain `net10.0` class library. Static `KeepAwake` class wrapping
  `SetThreadExecutionState` (kernel32). `Enable(keepDisplayOn)` sets
  `ES_CONTINUOUS|ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED` (+`ES_DISPLAY_REQUIRED`); `Disable()` sets `ES_CONTINUOUS`
  alone. Intentionally the minimal "ON forever / OFF" subset of PowerToys Awake — no timers.
  The execution state is per-thread, so `Enable`/`Disable` must be called from the same
  long-lived thread (the UI thread, via `KeepAwakeService` singleton).
- **`PowerModeSlider/`** — `net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0` WinUI 3 tray app. References
  `PowerModeLib`. Tray-only: `App.OnLaunched` creates `MainWindow` but never activates it
  (`AppWindow.Hide()`); there is no visible main window.

## Build / Run (winapp CLI — no Visual Studio needed)

This repo uses the [`winapp` CLI](https://github.com/microsoft/winappCli). The packaged app
**cannot build as `AnyCPU`** — always pass a runtime identifier.

```powershell
cd PowerModeSlider
dotnet run -r win-x64          # dotnet run is hooked into `winapp run` via Microsoft.Windows.SDK.BuildTools.WinApp
# or build then run manually:
dotnet build -c Debug -r win-x64
winapp run .\bin\Debug\net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0\win-x64
```

There are no automated tests or linters in this repo.

## Packaging (MSIX) — publisher must match the cert

`Package.appxmanifest` declares `Publisher="CN=gungaretti"`. The signing certificate's
subject **must match** that publisher and be trusted, or Windows refuses to install
(`0x800B010A` / `0x800B0109`). `winapp pack --generate-cert --install-cert` handles this in
one step. Bump `Version` in `Package.appxmanifest` before re-packing so Windows treats it as
an update. CI (`.github/workflows/release-msix.yml`) generates one shared self-signed cert in
a `cert` job and reuses it across the x64/arm64 matrix so the public `.cer` attached to the
release matches every architecture's MSIX.

## Conventions specific to this codebase

- **MVVM is the established pattern here** (this is C#/WinUI, not SwiftUI). UI logic lives in
  `ViewModels/PowerModeViewModel.cs` using `CommunityToolkit.Mvvm` source generators
  (`[ObservableProperty]`, `[RelayCommand]`, `partial` classes). Do not hand-roll
  `INotifyPropertyChanged`.
- **Dependency injection** is configured in `App.ConfigureServices()`
  (`Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection`). Services are interface-backed
  (`IPowerModeService` → `PowerModeService`) and resolved via
  `App.Current.Services.GetRequiredService<T>()`. Register new services/view-models there.
- **Power-mode flow:** ViewModel ↔ `IPowerModeService` ↔ `PowerModeLib.PowerMode`. The
  service sets *both* AC and DC modes for consistency and reads AC as the "current" mode. A
  single slider index (0/1/2) maps to Efficiency/Balanced/Performance throughout.
- **`PublishTrimmed=False` is intentional** — trimming strips WinUI XAML/`x:Bind` types and
  causes `0xc000027b` stowed-exception startup crashes in packaged/sideloaded builds. Keep it
  off. See the comment in `PowerModeSlider.csproj`.
- **Flyout window** (`FlyoutWindow`, a `WinUIEx.WindowEx`) uses heavy Win32 interop: a
  low-level `WH_MOUSE_LL` mouse hook for light-dismiss (WinUI 3 doesn't reliably fire
  deactivation), plus `DwmSetWindowAttribute` for rounded corners and manual positioning near
  the tray. The window instance is created once and reused.
- **Tray icon** comes from `WinUIEx.TrayIcon`. The icon `.ico` swaps with the selected mode
  (`MainWindow.UpdateTrayIcon`), driven by `ViewModel.PropertyChanged`. When keep-awake is on,
  the amber-badged `*Awake.ico` variant is shown instead. Those variants are generated by
  `scripts/Generate-AwakeIcons.ps1` (System.Drawing, PNG-in-ICO across all frame sizes) — rerun
  it if the base mode PNGs change.
- **"Start with Windows"** uses `Windows.ApplicationModel.StartupTask` (id
  `PowerModeSliderStartup`) and only works in packaged/MSIX builds; the code swallows the
  failure and hides the menu item on unpackaged runs.
- Both projects use nullable reference types enabled (`<Nullable>enable</Nullable>`).
